alabama.permitless_note: 18 for active-duty military and honorably discharged veterans.
alabama.duty_note: No duty to volunteer it. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
alabama.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
alabama.watch_out: A few places that are off-limits to permitless carriers (such as facilities hosting school or professional sporting events) remain open to people carrying with an actual pistol permit.
prohibited: Police, sheriff, and highway patrol stations
Jails and prisons
Courthouses and their annexes
District attorney offices
Buildings during county commission or city council meetings
Inpatient psychiatric facilities
Buildings with guards and screening at the entrances
School and college athletic event facilities (permit holders exempt)
K-12 school grounds — a felony if you intend to harm
Bars and restaurants are allowed; posted “no guns” signs have no force of law
alabama.nonres_note: No — residents only, with a military exception. Visitors 19+ can carry permitless anyway.

alaska.duty_note: You must tell an officer you are carrying immediately, on any contact — the officer may take and hold the handgun for the duration of the contact.
alaska.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
alaska.watch_out: On any contact with an officer you must immediately say you are carrying, and the officer may take and hold the handgun for the duration of the contact.
prohibited: K-12 schools
Child care facilities
Courthouses and court offices
Domestic violence and sexual assault shelters
Bars — any place licensed to serve alcohol on the premises (restaurants are OK if you are not drinking)
Another person’s home without their permission
alaska.nonres_note: No — but you don’t need one: Alaska is permitless at 21+.

arizona.duty_note: No duty to volunteer it. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
arizona.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
arizona.watch_out: Carrying concealed into a bar or restaurant that serves alcohol requires an actual concealed weapons permit (permitless carry does not count), the business must not post a no-weapons sign, and the carrier may not drink.
prohibited: School grounds
Polling places on election day
Nuclear and hydroelectric stations
Secured airport areas
Bars and restaurants that serve alcohol — permit holders may carry unless the place is posted; permitless carriers may not carry into places that serve alcohol
Tribal land has its own rules
arizona.nonres_note: Apply to the Department of Public Safety — same process as residents.

arkansas.duty_note: If you carry on a license, you must disclose that you are carrying when an officer asks for your identification.
arkansas.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
arkansas.watch_out: Only an Enhanced CHCL - not permitless carry and not a standard license - authorizes carry on public college campuses and into some other public buildings.
prohibited: K-12 schools
Law enforcement facilities
Courthouses and courtrooms
Detention facilities
Bars — alcohol-serving places that are not restaurants
Churches unless authorized
An Enhanced license opens public colleges, most public buildings, the Capitol, bars (unless posted), and churches (unless posted)
arkansas.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in Arkansas.

california.permitless_note: No — you need a California concealed carry weapon (CCW) license.
california.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
california.vehicle: Only unloaded and in a locked container.
california.watch_out: California bans magazines holding more than 10 rounds and treats many common semi-automatic rifles and handgun configurations as illegal 'assault weapons' - check the Department of Justice rules before bringing any firearm into the state.
prohibited: The “sensitive places” list in Penal Code § 26230: schools, child care, and colleges; government buildings; courthouses; hospitals and medical facilities
Bars and restaurants that serve alcohol, including their parking lots
Parks and playgrounds; libraries; museums; zoos; stadiums; places of worship; financial institutions; polling places; public transit
Several categories are under court injunction, and the private-property default was struck down in Wolford v. Lopez (June 2026) — check the current law before you carry
california.nonres_note: Effectively no general path — a 2025 court ruling (Hoffman v. Bonta) struck the residency bar, but so far relief covers only members of the organizations that sued. Most non-residents cannot get a California permit yet.

colorado.honors_fine_print: Resident permits only - the permit must be issued by the state where you live, you must be 21 or older, and you must also carry a matching state-issued driver's license or ID; nonresident permits are never recognized, and Colorado residents cannot carry in Colorado on another state's permit.
colorado.honored_in_fine_print: Minnesota: Only permits issued or renewed on or after August 1, 2024.
colorado.permitless_note: No — you need a Colorado concealed handgun permit.
colorado.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
colorado.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
colorado.watch_out: Colorado caps magazines at 15 rounds statewide (C.R.S. Sec. 18-12-302).
prohibited: K-12 schools
Colleges beyond parking lots
Child care facilities
The Capitol and legislative buildings
Courthouses
Local government buildings (SB 24-131 — a local government can opt out)
Polling places and ballot drop boxes
Public buildings with security screening
Bars and restaurants are allowed unless posted
colorado.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in Colorado.

connecticut.permitless_note: No — you need a Connecticut pistol permit.
connecticut.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
connecticut.watch_out: Connecticut bans magazines holding more than 10 rounds and most modern sporting rifles as 'assault weapons,' and has prohibited open carry since October 1, 2023.
prohibited: Schools
Legislative buildings
Court facilities and government buildings
State parks and forests
Hospitals
Posted private property
No statute bans carry in bars, restaurants, places of worship, sports arenas, or polling places
connecticut.nonres_note: Apply to the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection — you need a home-state permit first.

delaware.honors_fine_print: Idaho Enhanced permits only; North Dakota Class 1 permits only; South Dakota Enhanced permits only; Delaware honors both resident and non-resident licenses issued by the listed states.
delaware.permitless_note: No — you need a Delaware concealed deadly weapon (CCDW) license.
delaware.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
delaware.vehicle: Only openly - without a Delaware license or recognized permit, a loaded handgun in a vehicle must be in plain view (for example on the seat or dashboard); keeping it concealed, such as in a glove box, requires the license or recognized permit.
delaware.watch_out: The Attorney General re-issues the recognition list every January 15 and a state can be removed only on a year's notice - check the current AG list before a trip.
prohibited: Safe School and Recreation Zones — schools, recreation centers, athletic fields, and stadiums, and within 1,000 feet of them
Colleges
Courthouses
Police stations
Prisons and detention facilities
No ban on places of worship
delaware.nonres_note: Only a 30-day temporary permit for an employment need (11 Del. C. § 1441(k)).

florida.honored_in_fine_print: Wisconsin is a special case: it honors only Florida licenses issued to non-residents — a Florida resident's own license does not work there.
florida.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
florida.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
florida.watch_out: The places Florida law puts off-limits - schools, courthouses, bars, polling places, airport terminal buildings and others - are off-limits under permitless carry too.
prohibited: The 15 categories in § 790.06(12): police, sheriff, and highway patrol stations; jails and detention facilities; courthouses; polling places; government meetings
Schools, career centers, and colleges
The bar portion of an establishment that serves alcohol
Airport terminals
florida.nonres_note: The Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services issues non-resident Concealed Weapon/Firearm Licenses.

georgia.permitless_note: 18 for those who completed basic training and are on active duty or honorably discharged.
georgia.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
georgia.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
georgia.watch_out: Some places stay off-limits even for lawful weapons carriers, including courthouses, K-12 schools, and places of worship unless the governing body has chosen to allow carry.
prohibited: Courthouses
Jails and prisons
State mental health facilities
Nuclear power facilities
Within 150 feet of a polling place
Places of worship unless authorized
Government buildings with security screening
School safety zones (K-12; public-college campus carry except dorms and athletic facilities)
georgia.nonres_note: No general path — Weapons Carry Licenses go to Georgia residents only; active-duty military stationed in Georgia can also apply. Visitors don’t need one: Georgia is permitless for lawful weapons carriers 21+ (18+ military).

hawaii.permitless_note: No — you need a Hawaii license to carry.
hawaii.duty_note: You must immediately disclose that you are carrying when an officer stops you, or stops the vehicle you are riding in.
hawaii.vehicle: No — only unloaded and in an enclosed container under the 'place to keep' law; carrying or possessing a loaded firearm on a public highway is a separate offense.
hawaii.watch_out: Every firearm brought into Hawaii must be registered with the county chief of police within 5 days of arrival.
prohibited: Schools, child care, and colleges
Government buildings
Hospitals and medical facilities
Bars and restaurants that serve alcohol
Libraries; parks, beaches, and playgrounds; stadiums and theaters; polling places; banks; public transit and airports; shelters (HRS § 134-9.1)
Private property is no-carry by default unless the owner expressly allows it (HRS § 134-9.5, under Supreme Court review)
hawaii.nonres_note: No — Hawaii issues only to residents (HRS § 134-9).

idaho.inbound_note: Also honors every other state’s carry permit by law — carrying on a permit can matter for places permitless carry doesn’t reach, like some posted or restricted locations.
idaho.honored_in_fine_print: Delaware: Enhanced permit only; Minnesota: Enhanced permit only; Nevada: Enhanced permit only; Pennsylvania: Enhanced permit only; Washington: Enhanced permit only.
idaho.permitless_note: You must be a U.S. citizen or a current member of the U.S. Armed Forces.
idaho.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
idaho.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
idaho.watch_out: Permitless carry does not extend to public college and university campuses — carrying there requires an Idaho Enhanced License.
prohibited: Courthouses
Juvenile detention facilities
Jails
Public or private K-12 schools (an adult may keep a firearm locked in a vehicle on school property)
Public college dormitories and posted entertainment facilities seating 1,000+ (even for Enhanced licensees)
Permitless carry does not extend to public college campuses — that takes an Enhanced license
Bars and restaurants are allowed unless posted or you are under the influence
idaho.nonres_note: Apply in person to an Idaho county sheriff; for the Enhanced license you must have lived in Idaho six months or hold a current license from your home state.

illinois.permitless_note: No — you need an Illinois Concealed Carry License (CCL).
illinois.duty_note: You do not have to volunteer it, but during a stop you must tell the officer you are carrying if the officer asks.
illinois.vehicle: No — narrow exception: a non-resident who is eligible to carry in their home state (evidenced by a home-state license where applicable) may keep a loaded concealed handgun inside their vehicle, and must store it in the locked vehicle or a locked container if the vehicle is left unattended&hellip;
illinois.watch_out: The vehicle exception (430 ILCS 66/40(e)) covers the firearm only while it remains inside the vehicle — it does not authorize carrying on your person anywhere in Illinois.
prohibited: Schools and child care facilities, including parking areas
Colleges and universities
Government buildings and courthouses
Libraries
Public transit (buses and trains)
Public parks
Bars where alcohol is more than 50% of gross receipts
Stadiums and arenas; amusement parks, zoos, and museums; airports beyond security; casinos; polling places on election day; hospitals and medical facilities (430 ILCS 66/65)
illinois.nonres_note: Only residents of Arkansas, Idaho, Mississippi, Nevada, Texas, and Virginia — the states the Illinois State Police has found “substantially similar.” Everyone else has no path to an Illinois CCL (but a non-resident with a home-state permit may keep a loaded concealed handgun in a vehicle, 430 ILCS 66/40(e)).

indiana.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
indiana.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
prohibited: Schools and school buses
Courthouses
Airports and aircraft
Riverboat casinos
Federal buildings
Bars, restaurants, and places of worship are allowed
indiana.nonres_note: Only a five-year license, and only if you have a regular place of business or employment in Indiana.

iowa.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
iowa.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
iowa.watch_out: Permitless carry does not satisfy the federal Gun-Free School Zones Act exception, so DPS advises that an Iowa permit is still worth having — it also covers carry in other states.
prohibited: K-12 school grounds and the 1,000-foot zone around them
School buses
State university grounds
Casinos
Court buildings
Posted public buildings with guards
The Iowa State Fair
The Capitol complex (open carry banned)
Bars and restaurants are allowed unless posted; places of worship are allowed; posted signs have no force of law
iowa.nonres_note: Nonprofessional permits are residents-only; a professional permit is possible through the DPS Commissioner if your job requires carrying.

kansas.inbound_note: Also honors every other state’s carry permit by law — carrying on a permit can matter for places permitless carry doesn’t reach, like some posted or restricted locations.
kansas.permitless_note: Adults 18 to 20 may carry concealed only with a license Kansas recognizes — a Kansas provisional license or an out-of-state license.
kansas.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
kansas.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
kansas.watch_out: Kansas recognizes an out-of-state license only while the holder is not a Kansas resident (K.S.A. 75-7c03(c)) — someone who moves to Kansas must get a Kansas license or rely on permitless carry.
prohibited: K-12 schools
Courthouses with security
The state Capitol complex
State and municipal buildings with adequate security and posted notice
Colleges generally allow carry (campus carry)
Bars are allowed unless posted; posted signs mean you can be asked to leave, with no criminal penalty
Adults 18–20 need a provisional license
kansas.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in Kansas. Visitors 21+ can carry permitless anyway.

kentucky.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
kentucky.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
kentucky.watch_out: A person who moves to Kentucky holding a license from a state that has a reciprocity agreement with the Kentucky State Police may keep using that license for the first 120 days of residency, if they file the KSP form within 60 days of moving (KRS 237.110(20)(b)).
prohibited: Police stations and sheriff offices
Jails and prisons
Courthouses and courtrooms
Bar areas — places whose primary business is alcohol
K-12 schools and child care facilities
Colleges may ban carry by policy
Places of worship are allowed unless posted; restaurant dining areas are OK
kentucky.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in Kentucky. Visitors 21+ can carry permitless anyway.

louisiana.duty_note: Anyone carrying concealed, licensed or permitless, must inform an officer on contact, and must submit to a pat-down and let the officer temporarily disarm you.
louisiana.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
louisiana.watch_out: Louisiana's firearm-free school zones extend 1,000 feet beyond campus boundaries, and a concealed handgun may not be carried into another person's home without that person's consent.
prohibited: Law enforcement offices and stations
Courthouses and courtrooms
Polling places
The state Capitol
Places of worship unless authorized
Bars and Class A alcohol outlets (restaurants with a Class A-Restaurant permit are OK)
Schools, school buses, and firearm-free zones (1,000 feet)
Parades and demonstrations
Posted private property

maine.duty_note: Only if you are carrying without a permit — you must inform an officer immediately on contact. Permit holders are exempt from this duty.
maine.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
maine.watch_out: Loaded rifles and shotguns may not be carried in or on a motor vehicle (12 M.R.S. § 11212), even though a loaded handgun in the vehicle is allowed.
prohibited: Courthouses
Schools
The state Capitol area
State parks (concealed carry only with a permit; open carry banned)
Acadia National Park (permit required); Baxter State Park and the Allagash (park rules)
Bars and restaurants are allowed unless posted — and a posted sign carries criminal penalties (Class D crime)
Colleges set their own policy

maryland.permitless_note: No — you need a Maryland wear-and-carry permit.
maryland.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
maryland.vehicle: Only unloaded/locked — a handgun may be transported only unloaded and in an enclosed case or enclosed holster, and only between destinations the law allows, such as home, a target range, a gunsmith, or a place of business (Md. Code, Criminal Law § 4-203).
maryland.watch_out: Magazines holding more than 10 rounds cannot be sold, purchased, or transferred in Maryland, the Gun Safety Act of 2023 bans carry in a long list of sensitive places even for permit holders, and open carry is banned outright.
prohibited: Schools, preschools, and child care
Health care facilities
Government buildings
Higher-education buildings
Polling places
Power plants
State parks and forests
Stadiums, museums, amusement parks, racetracks, and casinos; MTA transit (Criminal Law § 4-111)

The bans on alcohol/cannabis establishments, the private-property default, and carrying within 1,000 feet of a demonstration are NOT currently enforced (Kipke v. Moore, stayed pending Supreme Court review; MSP update July 10, 2026)
Places of worship are not on the list
maryland.nonres_note: Apply to the Maryland State Police — same process as residents; fingerprints through a Maryland-approved LiveScan provider.

massachusetts.honored_in_fine_print: Minnesota: Only permits issued or renewed on or after August 1, 2024.
massachusetts.permitless_note: No — you need a Massachusetts License to Carry (LTC).
massachusetts.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
massachusetts.vehicle: No — without a Massachusetts LTC a loaded handgun in a vehicle is not lawful; transport is only unloaded/locked, apart from the narrow through-travel rule in the notes.
massachusetts.watch_out: A loaded firearm carried in a vehicle by a license holder must stay under the carrier's direct control (M.G.L. c.140, §131C(a)); a large-capacity rifle or shotgun in a vehicle must be unloaded and secured in a locked container (§131C(b)).
prohibited: Schools, colleges, and student transport
Government administration, court, and correctional buildings, including grounds and parking
Polling places and within 150 feet during voting
No specific ban on bars — but carrying with a BAC of .08 or higher, or under the influence, is banned
Posted signs mean trespass if you refuse to leave
massachusetts.nonres_note: A temporary one-year license from the Firearms Records Bureau / Colonel of State Police, $100 — it does not let you buy firearms.

michigan.inbound_note: Michigan honors every state’s carry permit — but only a resident permit: the permit must be issued by the state you live in. Nonresident permits are not honored.
michigan.permitless_note: No — you need a Michigan Concealed Pistol License (CPL).
michigan.duty_note: You must inform an officer that you are carrying during a stop or other official contact.
michigan.vehicle: No — without a Michigan CPL or a recognized home-state license, a pistol in a vehicle is treated as concealed carry; a pistol may only be transported unloaded, in a closed case, in the trunk (or not readily accessible if there is no trunk) for a lawful purpose.
michigan.watch_out: Michigan's pistol-free zones (MCL 28.425o — schools, hospitals and other listed premises) apply to out-of-state carriers as well as Michigan CPL holders.
prohibited: The pistol-free zones in MCL 28.425o: schools; child care; sports arenas; bars (primary alcohol income); places of worship unless the presiding official allows it
Entertainment facilities seating 2,500+; hospitals; college classrooms and dorms; casinos
Parking lots are excluded
michigan.nonres_note: Only active-duty military stationed in Michigan.

minnesota.honors_fine_print: Enhanced permits only for Idaho, Mississippi, Montana, South Dakota and Tennessee; North Dakota Class 1 license only; Colorado and Massachusetts permits only if issued or renewed on or after August 1, 2024. The holder must not be prohibited by law from possessing a firearm (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 16(b)).
minnesota.permitless_note: No — you need a Minnesota Permit to Carry.
minnesota.duty_note: A permit holder must disclose whether they are carrying when a peace officer asks (Minn. Stat. § 624.714, subd. 1b(d)). You do not have to volunteer it unasked.
minnesota.vehicle: No — without a permit Minnesota issues or honors, a handgun in a vehicle must be unloaded and in a closed, fastened case/gunbox or securely tied package, or unloaded in the closed trunk; loaded vehicle carry requires a recognized permit.
minnesota.watch_out: Without a Minnesota-issued or recognized permit, a firearm in a motor vehicle must be unloaded and in a gun case that fully encloses it and is zipped, snapped, buckled, tied or otherwise fastened, or unloaded in the closed trunk (Minn. Stat. 97B.045).
prohibited: K-12 school property (with a parking-lot exception)
Courthouses — a statewide court order since September 1, 2026 bans firearms in court facilities
The state Capitol and legislative buildings
Child care centers
State correctional facilities and state hospitals
The Minnesota Zoo
State game refuges
Private establishments with a compliant posted notice or verbal notice
Bars and restaurants that serve alcohol — only if you are drinking or under the influence (§ 624.714, subd. 17; § 609.66)

mississippi.inbound_note: Also honors every other state’s carry permit by law — carrying on a permit can matter for places permitless carry doesn’t reach, like some posted or restricted locations.
mississippi.honored_in_fine_print: Minnesota: Enhanced permit only; Nevada: Enhanced permit only.
mississippi.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
mississippi.vehicle: Yes — any person over the age of 18 may carry a firearm concealed in whole or in part within any motor vehicle without a permit (Miss. Code 97-37-1(2), quoted on the Mississippi DPS FAQ); the statute sets no unloaded or locked-container requirement.
prohibited: Places of nuisance; police, sheriff, and highway patrol stations; detention facilities, prisons, and jails
Courthouses and courtrooms; polling places; government-body meetings and Legislature meetings
School, college, and professional athletic events; bar portions of alcohol-serving establishments
Elementary and secondary schools; junior colleges, community colleges, and universities
Churches and places of worship; airport passenger terminals; posted private property (§ 45-9-101(13))
An Enhanced endorsement opens most of these — but not nuisance places, police stations, jails and prisons, or courtrooms during proceedings
mississippi.nonres_note: A standard permit can go to a non-resident who already holds a valid permit from another state, or to military stationed in Mississippi; the Enhanced endorsement is for residents only.

missouri.inbound_note: Also honors every other state’s carry permit by law — carrying on a permit can matter for places permitless carry doesn’t reach, like some posted or restricted locations.
missouri.honored_in_fine_print: Wisconsin: Regular license only — provisional licenses are not honored.
missouri.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
missouri.vehicle: Yes — a loaded concealable firearm may be carried in the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle at 19+ (18+ military), if otherwise lawfully possessed.
missouri.watch_out: Missouri has a long list of restricted places under RSMo 571.107 (schools, courthouses/courtrooms, polling places, hospitals, stadiums seating 5,000+, bars primarily devoted to liquor sales, and private property posted with 11x14-inch signs)&hellip;
prohibited: Police, sheriff, and highway patrol stations
Within 25 feet of a polling place on election day
Jails and prisons; courthouses and court offices; government meetings
Bar areas without consent
Secured airport areas; schools and colleges without consent; child care facilities
Riverboat casinos without consent; gated amusement park areas; churches without consent; posted private property
Arenas and stadiums seating 5,000+; hospitals open to the public (RSMo 571.107)
A permit holder who enters one of these places commits no criminal act under that section — but can still be asked to leave and lose the permit; permitless carriers face criminal charges
missouri.nonres_note: No — residents or military stationed in Missouri. Visitors 19+ can carry permitless anyway.

montana.honored_in_fine_print: Minnesota: Enhanced permit only; Washington: Enhanced permit only.
montana.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
montana.vehicle: Yes — Montana Dept. of Justice: 'Montana has no prohibitions about carrying a weapon in a motor vehicle'.
montana.watch_out: A permit still matters for government buildings: under MCA 45-8-328 a person without a Montana permit (MCA 45-8-321/45-8-312) or a permit recognized under MCA 45-8-329 commits an offense by carrying concealed in restricted portions of a building used for state or local government offices; the Dept.
prohibited: School buildings
Courtrooms and court-controlled spaces
Restricted portions of state and local government office buildings (permit holders are exempt)
Secure treatment facilities
Federal buildings
Universities under Board of Regents policy
Private property where prohibited
Bars and restaurants are allowed if you are not under the influence
montana.nonres_note: No — Montana issues only to residents. Visitors 18+ can carry permitless anyway.

nebraska.duty_note: You must inform an officer — and emergency medical staff — that you are carrying during official contact.
nebraska.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
nebraska.watch_out: Carry is barred in many listed places — schools, financial institutions, hospitals/emergency rooms, establishments deriving over half their income from liquor sales, and any posted premises — and in a prohibited place's public parking lot the handgun must be locked inside the glove box, trunk&hellip;
prohibited: Police, sheriff, and State Patrol stations
Detention facilities, prisons, and jails
Courtrooms and buildings with a courtroom
Polling places during an election; government-body meetings; Legislature meetings
Financial institutions
Professional and semi-professional athletic events
School buildings, grounds, vehicles, and sponsored activities
Places of worship (which may authorize their own security with written notice to the congregation)
Hospitals, emergency rooms, and trauma centers
Political rallies and fundraisers; establishments deriving more than 50% of income from alcohol; posted premises (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 28-1202.01, LB 1237, effective July 18, 2026)
nebraska.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in Nebraska and their spouses.

nevada.honors_fine_print: Idaho, Mississippi, and South Dakota: Enhanced permits only; North Dakota: Class 1 permits only. A person who becomes a Nevada resident may no longer carry on the out-of-state permit unless issued a Nevada sheriff's permit within 60 days of becoming a resident (NRS 202.3688(2)).
nevada.permitless_note: No — you need a Nevada CCW permit.
nevada.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
nevada.vehicle: Yes — if the handgun is not concealed on your person; concealed on your person in the vehicle requires a recognized permit.
nevada.watch_out: Long guns are treated differently in a vehicle: it is unlawful to carry a loaded rifle or shotgun in or on a vehicle on a public highway or other public way, and 'loaded' means a round in the firing chamber — rounds only in the magazine do not count (NRS 503.165).
prohibited: K-12 schools
Child care
College campuses
Public buildings with metal detectors or posted signs
Prisons
Bars and restaurants are allowed if you are not intoxicated and the place is not posted; casinos are private property and nearly all prohibit firearms
nevada.nonres_note: Apply in person to any county sheriff.

new-hampshire.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
new-hampshire.vehicle: Yes — a loaded handgun may be carried in a vehicle, openly or concealed, loaded or unloaded, with no permit.
new-hampshire.watch_out: Firearms are barred in a courtroom or any area used by a court (RSA 159:19), whether the carrier is licensed or unlicensed.
prohibited: Courtrooms and any area used by a court (RSA 159:19 — a Class B felony)
Prisons and detention facilities
Posted private property
Bars and restaurants are allowed

Schools: state law targets students, but the federal Gun-Free School Zones Act still applies within 1,000 feet of a school — only a state-issued license gives you the federal exception, so carrying without the optional NH license near a school is a federal risk
new-hampshire.nonres_note: Apply to the New Hampshire State Police — $100, five years.
new-hampshire.source_label: Official source: New Hampshire's permit-recognition page →

new-jersey.permitless_note: No — you need a New Jersey permit to carry.
new-jersey.duty_note: You must inform an officer that you are carrying during a stop or other official contact.
new-jersey.vehicle: Only unloaded/locked — without a New Jersey carry permit a handgun may only be transported unloaded in a closed and fastened case, gun box, or securely tied package, or locked in the trunk, and only for exempt purposes/direct travel.
new-jersey.watch_out: Magazines holding more than 10 rounds are banned — possession is a fourth-degree crime (N.J.S.A. 2C:39-1y and 2C:39-3(j)) — and transport rules are strictly enforced with no unreasonable deviations from the direct route allowed.
prohibited: Schools, colleges, and child care
Government buildings and courts
Public transit
Parks, beaches, and playgrounds
Bars and restaurants that serve alcohol
Health care facilities
Libraries and museums
Casinos; entertainment venues, stadiums, arenas, and racetracks (N.J.S.A. 2C:58-4.6; 2C:39-5(e))
The private-property default rule is not currently enforced for property open to the public (NJSP notice, December 11, 2025; Koons litigation pending)
Places of worship are not on the list
new-jersey.nonres_note: Apply online through a New Jersey State Police station — same standards as residents; two-year permit.
new-jersey.source_label: Official source: New Jersey's permit-recognition page →

new-mexico.honors_fine_print: Must be 21+; recognition is for non-residents visiting or passing through — New Mexico residents must hold a New Mexico license.
new-mexico.permitless_note: No — you need a New Mexico concealed handgun license.
new-mexico.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
new-mexico.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
new-mexico.watch_out: Your license is not valid on tribal land unless the tribe or pueblo has authorized it (NMSA 29-19-10), and a large share of northwestern New Mexico is tribal land.
prohibited: K-12 schools
Universities
Preschools
Courts
Tribal land
Public buses
Polling places within 100 feet
Bars with a dispenser’s license (restaurants serving beer and wine may be OK)
State parks are OK for license holders
new-mexico.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in New Mexico.
new-mexico.source_label: Official source: New Mexico's permit-recognition page →

new-york.permitless_note: No — you need a New York pistol license.
new-york.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
new-york.watch_out: Even a New York license issued outside New York City is not valid inside NYC without a special permit from the NYPD police commissioner (Penal Law 400.00(6)), the Concealed Carry Improvement Act bans carry in a long list of 'sensitive locations,' and magazines are limited to 10 rounds.
prohibited: The “sensitive locations” in Penal Law § 265.01-e: government buildings and courthouses; health care facilities and places of worship; schools, colleges, libraries, public parks, playgrounds, and zoos
The entire public transit system — subways, buses, ferries, airports, train and bus terminals
Bars and restaurants licensed for on-premises alcohol or cannabis consumption; the Times Square gun-free zone
Private property is no-carry by default unless the owner posts clear signage permitting firearms or gives express consent (§ 265.01-d)
Carrying in a sensitive location is a class E felony even with a license
A license issued outside New York City is not valid inside the five boroughs without a special NYPD permit
new-york.nonres_note: Limited — non-residents can apply for a New York City carry license through the NYPD (38 RCNY § 5-03(b)); outside the city, generally only part-time residents or people employed in New York.
new-york.source_label: New York State’s official gun safety page

north-carolina.inbound_note: North Carolina honors every state’s carry permit by statute. You must carry the permit and a valid photo ID at all times, and North Carolina’s own carry restrictions apply to you while you are here.
north-carolina.permitless_note: No — a permit is still required. A permitless-carry bill (Senate Bill 50) was vetoed in June 2025; the Senate overrode the veto, but the House has never taken the override vote. See the note at the bottom of this section.
north-carolina.duty_note: You must inform an officer that you are carrying during a stop or other official contact.
north-carolina.vehicle: No — without a permit this state issues or honors, use the locked-transport rules below.
north-carolina.watch_out: Posted 'no concealed weapons' signs have the force of law, carry is barred at parades, funeral processions, pickets and demonstrations, and you may not carry while consuming alcohol or under the influence.
prohibited: Educational property — K-12 and colleges (G.S. 14-269.2, a Class I felony)
Courthouses and Capitol grounds
Law enforcement and correctional facilities
Assemblies, parades, funerals, and demonstrations
Posted private property
Bars and alcohol venues — permit holders may carry in restaurants while sober and not drinking
Places of worship that host schools are allowed outside school hours if a private school
north-carolina.nonres_note: No — except military stationed in North Carolina. You need a North Carolina permit to carry here.
north-carolina.special: PENDING — Senate Bill 50, the “Freedom to Carry NC” permitless-carry bill, was vetoed by the governor in June 2025. The Senate overrode the veto, but the House has never taken the override vote; the last chances are the November 16 and November 30, 2026 sessions. A permit is still required in North Carolina as of November 2026.
north-carolina.source_label: Official source: North Carolina's permit-recognition page →

north-dakota.honored_in_fine_print: Delaware: Class 1 license only; Minnesota: Class 1 license only; Nevada: Class 1 license only; Pennsylvania: Class 1 license only; Washington: Class 1 license only.
north-dakota.permitless_note: You must carry a valid driver’s license or state ID.
north-dakota.duty_note: If you are carrying without a permit, you must tell the officer you are carrying only if the officer asks about it (N.D.C.C. § 62.1-04-04). If you carry on a license, show it if the officer asks to see it.
north-dakota.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
north-dakota.watch_out: Constitutional carry works only inside North Dakota — the moment you cross the state line you need an actual North Dakota concealed weapon license for reciprocity to apply.
prohibited: K-12 schools and school-sponsored events
Places of worship unless the religious leader or governing body approves
Bar or lounge areas of alcohol-serving establishments
Publicly owned or operated buildings (city halls, courthouses)
Gaming sites where bingo is the primary game
State game refuges; Capitol buildings and grounds
Violating this list is a noncriminal offense with a $100 fee (N.D.C.C. § 62.1-02-05)
north-dakota.nonres_note: Yes, with conditions — you must hold a valid license from your home state (one with North Dakota reciprocity) and complete North Dakota’s testing in North Dakota.
north-dakota.source_label: Official source: North Dakota's permit-recognition page →

ohio.duty_note: You do not have to volunteer it, but if the officer asks whether you are carrying, you must answer.
ohio.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
ohio.watch_out: 'No firearms' signs posted by a business or property owner carry the force of law in Ohio — carrying past one is criminal trespass.
prohibited: Police and sheriff stations
Courthouses and buildings containing courtrooms
School safety zones (license holders have a vehicle exception; permitless carriers risk the federal Gun-Free School Zones Act)
Colleges and universities unless authorized
Places of worship unless authorized
Government facilities unless authorized
Liquor premises — only if you are not drinking (ORC 2923.126)
Posted signs carry the force of law
ohio.nonres_note: Only non-residents who work in Ohio.

oklahoma.permitless_note: 18 for members and veterans of the Armed Forces, Reserves, and National Guard.
oklahoma.duty_note: You do not have to volunteer it. If the officer asks, you must tell them (21 O.S. § 1290.8).
oklahoma.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
oklahoma.watch_out: You must have a handgun license, military ID, driver's license, or state photo ID on you whenever you carry, and businesses whose primary purpose is serving alcohol are off-limits.
prohibited: Schools (K-12, buses), colleges and technology centers (unless authorized; vehicle storage exception)
Courthouses
Government buildings used for public business; government meetings
Jails and prisons
Bars — businesses whose primary purpose is on-premises alcohol
Places of worship unless posted or on notice
Sports arenas and gambling venues (with parking exceptions)
Posted private property (21 O.S. § 1277)
Restaurant areas are OK if you are not under the influence
oklahoma.nonres_note: No general program — SDA licenses go to residents and military stationed in Oklahoma; some non-residents employed in Oklahoma may qualify. Visitors 21+ can carry permitless anyway.

oregon.permitless_note: No — you need an Oregon concealed handgun license.
oregon.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly.
oregon.vehicle: Only if openly visible or locked away.
oregon.watch_out: Cities and counties may restrict possession of loaded firearms in public places by local ordinance (ORS 166.173) — Portland and several other cities do — so even openly carrying a loaded handgun can be restricted locally.
prohibited: Court facilities
The State Capitol
Airport terminals
Schools and colleges with posted policy
Local government meeting buildings with posted policy
Bars and restaurants are allowed unless posted; places of worship are allowed unless posted
Oregon honors no out-of-state permits
oregon.nonres_note: Only residents of bordering states (Washington, Idaho, California, Nevada) who show a compelling need.

pennsylvania.honors_fine_print: Resident permits only — you must be a resident of the state that issued your license; must be 21 or older; Idaho: Enhanced license only; North Dakota: Class 1 license only; Utah: Regular license only.
pennsylvania.permitless_note: No — you need a Pennsylvania License to Carry Firearms.
pennsylvania.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
pennsylvania.vehicle: No — without a permit this state issues or honors, use the locked-transport rules below.
pennsylvania.watch_out: Philadelphia is the exception to Pennsylvania's open-carry rule: carrying a firearm openly in Philadelphia requires a License to Carry Firearms (18 Pa.C.S. 6108), even though no license is needed for open carry elsewhere in the state.
prohibited: K-12 schools
Court facilities (lockers are provided)
Detention and correctional facilities
Mental health institutions
The State Capitol Complex
No state ban on bars or restaurants
Philadelphia: open carry needs a License to Carry Firearms (a June 2025 Superior Court ruling found that requirement unconstitutional — status unsettled)
pennsylvania.nonres_note: Apply to a county sheriff — you must hold your home-state permit; not all sheriffs issue to non-residents.

rhode-island.permitless_note: No — you need a Rhode Island pistol permit.
rhode-island.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
rhode-island.watch_out: Rhode Island's only break for out-of-state permit holders is pass-through: section 11-47-8 lets you drive through the state with a pistol in your vehicle if you are merely transporting it through Rhode Island with no intent to stop or stay — it is not a right to carry while visiting.
prohibited: K-12 school grounds
State and national parks, forests, and wildlife management areas
Courthouses and government facilities
Airports
Bars and restaurants are allowed if not posted and you are not under the influence; places of worship are allowed
rhode-island.nonres_note: Apply locally (§ 11-47-11) if you hold a home-state permit, or to the Attorney General (§ 11-47-18).
rhode-island.source_label: Official source: Rhode Island's permit-recognition page →

south-carolina.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
south-carolina.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
south-carolina.watch_out: 'No Concealable Weapons Allowed' signs carry legal force, and carry is prohibited in schools, courthouses, law-enforcement and detention facilities, hospitals and places where medical procedures are performed, churches unless the governing body allows it, and polling places on election days.
prohibited: Law enforcement, correctional, and detention facilities
Courthouses and courtrooms while court is in session
Polling places on election day
Government-body meetings
School and college athletic events not related to firearms
Daycare and preschool facilities
Hospitals, medical clinics, and doctors’ offices
Churches and religious sanctuaries unless permission is given
The state Capitol grounds; posted premises (§ 16-23-20)
K-12 school property is a felony (locked-vehicle exception); colleges are covered by a separate law (§ 16-23-420)
Bars and restaurants are allowed if you do not drink while carrying
south-carolina.nonres_note: Only a “qualified nonresident” — someone who owns real property in South Carolina, or military stationed there.
south-carolina.source_label: Official source: South Carolina's permit-recognition page →

south-dakota.honored_in_fine_print: Delaware: Enhanced permit only; Minnesota: Enhanced permit only; Nevada: Enhanced permit only; Washington: Enhanced or Gold permit only — the regular permit is not honored.
south-dakota.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly.
south-dakota.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
south-dakota.watch_out: Carry in the State Capitol is limited to enhanced-permit holders; courthouses and K-12 schools are off-limits.
prohibited: K-12 schools (SDCL 13-32-7)
County courthouses and the state Capitol (SDCL 22-14-23 — an Enhanced permit plus 24 hours’ notice to the Highway Patrol superintendent is the one exception for the Capitol)
Establishments deriving more than half their income from alcohol
Game preserves and refuges
Posted signs have no force of law (trespass only)
An Enhanced permit opens courthouses and school property (with restrictions)
south-dakota.nonres_note: No general non-resident permits; military stationed in South Dakota and their spouses can apply. Visitors 18+ can carry permitless anyway.
south-dakota.source_label: Official source: South Dakota's permit-recognition page →

tennessee.inbound_note: Also honors every other state’s carry permit by law — carrying on a permit can matter for places permitless carry doesn’t reach, like some posted or restricted locations.
tennessee.permitless_note: The statute still reads 21+, but a January 2023 federal court order bars Tennessee from enforcing the higher age — in practice, 18 and older.
tennessee.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. You only have to show your permit if an officer asks while you are carrying in a place or way that is legal only because you have the permit.
tennessee.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
tennessee.watch_out: Out-of-state permit holders must keep the permit on their person while carrying; anyone who becomes a Tennessee resident must obtain a Tennessee permit within 6 months.
prohibited: K-12 schools and school buses
Colleges and universities (students and the general public; faculty exceptions)
Courthouses and buildings where judicial proceedings are held (a Class E felony)
Government buildings posted weapons-free
Public parks, playgrounds, and civic centers
Penal institutions; TVA recreational lands
Posted private property (signs carry the force of law, § 39-17-1359)
Bars and restaurants: no specific ban, but carrying while under the influence is a crime (§ 39-17-1321)
tennessee.nonres_note: No general non-resident permits; an out-of-state permit holder employed in Tennessee at least 30 hours a week for at least six months can apply for an eight-year Enhanced permit. Visitors 18+ can carry permitless anyway.

texas.duty_note: If you carry on a License to Carry, you must display it when an officer demands your ID. There is no equivalent display duty for permitless carriers.
texas.vehicle: Yes - the handgun must not be in plain view (or must be in a holster).
texas.watch_out: Some locations open to LTC holders remain off-limits to permitless carriers, and 30.06/30.07 signs can bar license holders from private property.
prohibited: Schools and school buses
Courts and court offices
Polling places on election day and during early voting
Racetracks
Secured airport areas
51% establishments — businesses that derive 51% or more of income from on-premises alcohol sales (look for the red “51%” sign)
High school and collegiate sporting events; correctional facilities
Hospitals, nursing homes, amusement parks, and government meetings with proper notice (Penal Code §§ 46.03, 46.035)
Colleges: license holders may carry on campus; permitless carriers may not carry in college buildings
Private property owners can bar carry with 30.06 (concealed) and 30.07 (open) signs
texas.nonres_note: Apply to the Department of Public Safety (Gov’t Code § 411.173).

utah.inbound_note: Also honors every other state’s carry permit by law — carrying on a permit can matter for places permitless carry doesn’t reach, like some posted or restricted locations.
utah.honored_in_fine_print: Pennsylvania: Regular license only — the provisional (18–20) license is not honored; Washington: Provisional (18–20) permit not honored.
utah.permitless_note: 18 to 20 with a Utah provisional permit.
utah.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly.
utah.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
prohibited: K-12 schools (permitless carriers and out-of-state-only holders are barred; Utah CFP holders are exempt)
Secure areas — courthouses with security, correctional and law enforcement facilities
Airport secure areas
Houses of worship and private residences if posted notice is given (an infraction)
Colleges are allowed at 21+
Bars are not listed as banned
utah.nonres_note: Apply to the Bureau of Criminal Identification — you need a home-state permit if your home state recognizes Utah’s.

vermont.permitless_note: Vermont has never had a permit system and sets no minimum age of its own — but federal law bars handgun possession under 18.
vermont.duty_note: No — Vermont law does not require you to volunteer that you are carrying. If an officer asks, answer honestly.
vermont.vehicle: Yes for handguns - but carrying a loaded rifle or shotgun in a motor vehicle is prohibited (10 V.S.A. 4705).
vermont.watch_out: Vermont bans the sale/transfer of magazines holding over 15 rounds (handguns) or 10 rounds (long guns); magazines lawfully possessed before Oct. 1, 2018 are grandfathered.
prohibited: School buildings and school buses (§ 4004)
Courthouses (§ 4016)
Hospital buildings (§ 4023, posted)
Polling places and their walkways on election day (§ 4027, firearms stored in a vehicle excepted)
State buildings
State institutions and residential treatment programs
Center-based child care and preschool programs
Colleges and universities by policy
Bars and restaurants are allowed; places of worship are allowed unless posted
vermont.nonres_note: There is no Vermont permit to get — anyone who can legally possess a firearm may carry here, resident or visitor.

virginia.inbound_note: Virginia honors every state’s concealed handgun permit (handguns only). You must be 21 or older, carry government-issued photo ID, and show your permit and ID when an officer demands them.
virginia.honored_in_fine_print: Wisconsin is a special case: it honors only Virginia permits issued to non-residents — a Virginia resident's own permit does not work there.
virginia.permitless_note: No — you need a Virginia concealed handgun permit.
virginia.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
virginia.vehicle: Yes - no permit needed for a handgun in a personal vehicle if it is secured in a container or compartment; the compartment does not have to be locked.
virginia.watch_out: Open carry is legal without a permit; some counties regulate carrying loaded rifles or shotguns on public highways.
prohibited: K-12 schools
Courthouses
The Capitol Building and Square and state government buildings
Airport terminals
Places of worship during services without good reason
Polling places within 40 feet on election day
Local government buildings and parks where the locality bans carry
Bars and restaurants are allowed, but no drinking while carrying concealed (§ 18.2-308.012)
virginia.nonres_note: Apply to the Virginia State Police (§ 18.2-308.06).
virginia.special: CHANGING SOON — Senate Bill 115 (Chapter 879, 2026 Acts of Assembly) ends Virginia’s automatic recognition of every state’s permit. The State Police must drop states that don’t meet Virginia’s new “substantially similar” standard by December 1, 2026, and from July 1, 2027 a Virginia resident can no longer carry on another state’s permit (active-duty military and spouses excepted). The list above is current as of November 2026 — check the State Police page before you travel.

washington.honors_fine_print: Only these 10 states, and only specific permit types: Idaho Enhanced permit only; Kansas standard license only; Montana Enhanced only (temporarily restricted enhanced permits issued to 18-20 year olds are not recognized); North Dakota Class 1 permits only&hellip;
washington.permitless_note: No — you need a Washington Concealed Pistol License (CPL).
washington.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
washington.vehicle: No - a loaded pistol in a vehicle requires a concealed pistol license; an unloaded pistol may be transported/left in a vehicle only if locked within the vehicle and concealed from view (RCW 9.41.050).
washington.watch_out: Washington bans the sale (not possession) of magazines over 10 rounds and of many semi-automatic rifles; items lawfully owned before the bans are generally grandfathered.
prohibited: K-12 schools, grounds, and buses (a narrow exception for license holders picking up or dropping off a student, firearm secured in the vehicle)
Child care centers
Court facilities (courtrooms, jury rooms, judges’ chambers)
Restricted areas of jails and police stations
Restricted areas of mental health facilities
Bars and taverns (areas off-limits to people under 21)
Public libraries; accredited zoos and aquariums; transit stations; parks (RCW 9.41.300, 9.41.280, 9.41.282; SB 5444 expansion, mid-2025)
Open carry is banned at the state Capitol and at city or county council meetings; concealed carry with a CPL is allowed
washington.nonres_note: Apply in person at any sheriff’s office — about $51, five years; a training requirement takes effect May 1, 2027.

west-virginia.honored_in_fine_print: Wisconsin: Regular license only — provisional licenses are not honored.
west-virginia.permitless_note: Since June 12, 2026 (HB 4106), any U.S. citizen or legal resident 18 or older who is not prohibited may carry concealed without a license. The old 21+ rule and the provisional license for 18- to 20-year-olds are gone (W. Va. Code § 61-7-7(c)).
west-virginia.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly.
west-virginia.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
prohibited: K-12 schools, school buses, and school functions (a license holder may keep a concealed handgun in a vehicle in a school parking lot or traffic circle)
Courthouses and court premises
The State Capitol Complex (buildings and grounds; vehicle carry in the complex is permitted)
Correctional facilities
Bars and restaurants: no state ban — allowed unless posted
west-virginia.source_label: Official source: West Virginia's permit-recognition page →

wisconsin.honors_fine_print: Holder must be at least 21 and must NOT be a Wisconsin resident - Wisconsin residents need a Wisconsin license even if they hold another state's. Special conditions: Florida and Virginia NON-RESIDENT licenses only (their resident licenses do not qualify); Idaho regular or enhanced licenses only (emergency licenses excluded)&hellip;
wisconsin.permitless_note: No — you need a Wisconsin CCW license.
wisconsin.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
wisconsin.vehicle: Only unloaded and encased, unless the carrier holds a license recognized by Wisconsin.
wisconsin.watch_out: Recognition turns on the other state's background check being comparable to Wisconsin's (criminal-history search plus NICS), per Wis. Admin. Code Jus 17.13 - which is why a few states' licenses (ME, NJ, OR) fail to qualify.
prohibited: Police, sheriff, and State Patrol stations
Prisons, jails, and secured correctional facilities
Secure mental health facilities
Courthouses
Municipal courtrooms while court is in session
Secured airport areas
School grounds (§ 948.605 — licensees are exempt from the 1,000-foot zone but not the grounds; unloaded/encased transport exceptions apply)
Colleges and universities if posted
Taverns only if you are not drinking
Posted private property (§ 175.60(16))
wisconsin.nonres_note: No — only military stationed in Wisconsin. Out-of-state civilians rely on reciprocity.

wyoming.permitless_note: Any U.S. resident 21 or older who can legally possess a firearm (since July 1, 2021). A Wyoming permit itself is now available at 18+ (HB 96, effective July 1, 2026).
wyoming.duty_note: No law requires you to volunteer that you are carrying. If the officer asks, answer honestly, and show your permit and ID when asked for them.
wyoming.vehicle: Yes — no permit is needed for a handgun in your vehicle.
prohibited: Law enforcement facilities (without the chief administrator’s written consent)
Detention facilities, prisons, and jails
Courtrooms (the presiding judge decides)
The bar portion of an alcohol-serving establishment
School, college, and professional athletic events not related to firearms
Public schools and colleges: you need a permit — permitless carriers may not carry there (W.S. 6-8-104(t)); the 2025 gun-free-zone repeal (HB 172) opened them to permit holders
wyoming.nonres_note: No — Wyoming does not issue permits to non-residents (DCI FAQ). Visitors 21+ can carry permitless anyway.
